title: Different Colour Space Used in Visual Shader ColorParameter Depending on Qualifier Setting
body:
### Tested versions

- Tested in v4.3.stable.steam [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Windows 11 - Vulkan (Forward+) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12/24-Core CPU

### Issue description

I am not certain if this is a bug or not, plus I am not certain if this is related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101605 or the apparent fix https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101642 , but I wanted to point it out just in case because it FEELS like a bug and I was unable to find mention of this exact problem.

For some curious reason, within a 3D project, if I attach a ColorParameter in a Visual Shader and leave its qualifier set to None, it works as expected. However, if I set the qualifier as Instance, it will produce different results given the exact same colours applied to it, taking into account that None attaches the parameter to the shader resource and Instance attaches the parameter to the visual instance node containing the material resource the shader resource is attached to.

For the moment, a workaround is simply to use a Vector3Parameter instead, though I have noted that if changes are made to Instance parameters in a shader, all instances where those Instance parameters are used need to be changed to something different and changed back for those changes to be properly applied. (That's not a bug, just an easy thing to miss when testing this.)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new project, make your starting world a Node3D, add a MeshInstance3D, give it a default Cube mesh.
2. Duplicate the cube and move it to a different position so you can see both cubes.
3. Put a new shader material into the Material Override slot of MeshInstance3D and create a new Visual Shader to go with it.
4. Edit the visual shader and create a ColorParameter node. Give it a default colour of 64,192,64,255 as this is an easy colour to see the difference with.
5. Attach the ColorParameter to Albedo.
6. Repeat steps 3 through 5 with MeshInstance3D2, but before you attach the ColorParameter to Albedo, set the Qualifier to "Instance".
7. Both cubes should look different despite having the exact same colour fed to Albedo.
